summary: Pulaski County, IN steel fire tower announced in 1933 at 80 ft for the Jasper-Pulaski game preserve; gone, and its spot is now a parking lot per a 2023 visit.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, announced at 80 feet in October 1933
facts.status_note: Indiana Fire Towers: not standing and no evidence remains; FFLA list: gone; spot is a parking lot per the author's December 2023 visit
facts.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources (listed as a DNR fire tower in the Forest Service list)

access.note: Now the Jasper-Pulaski Fish & Wildlife Area; hunters, range users and dog runners must get a one-day access permit before entering the field, and DNR encourages other visitors to get one

events.note: Acquisition of the land for Jasper-Pulaski began
Announced in October 1933: a steel fire tower, 80 feet tall, to be erected on the game preserve by Civilian Conservation Corps workers; one of six assigned to Indiana
Outdoor Indiana (May 1934) article on the preserve with a photo of a fire tower
Author asked a DNR employee at Tippecanoe River State Park, who confirmed the location and said no remnant of the tower remains
Author's December 2023 visit found the tower location is now a parking lot

notes_for_editor: Brief record height_m 24.4 equals the announced 80 ft; it is a planned height, not a measured one. Build date is not confirmed; the May 1934 magazine photo is the earliest evidence of a standing tower. The parking-lot location rests on one author's 2023 visit and his 2022 conversation with a DNR employee, so a second check would help. The Indiana Fire Towers author notes the state's 1939 magazine cover shows the tower, but that image is not cited here. A modern observation area for sandhill cranes exists on the property; sources read do not link any tower there to the fire tower, and the DNR PDF text was too garbled to quote, so it is not mentioned in the story.
